_comment: Lighthouse CI. Replaces a lighthouserc.js that was dead three times over:
it used module.exports in a "type": "module" package so it could never
load, every assertion was "warn" so it could never fail, and it set both
`url` and `staticDistDir`. JSON is used here so there is no module system
to get wrong.
RUN THIS AGAINST A DEPLOYED ORIGIN, NEVER LOCALHOST. Re-measured
2026-07-30, desktop preset, 3 runs each:
local `npm run start`  perf 100  TBT   0ms   <- meaningless as a gate
SWA preview origin     perf  97  TBT   0ms
apex bridgingtrust.ai  perf  81  TBT 293ms
A localhost gate scores a perfect 100 while real users get 81. It would
pass forever and detect nothing, which is the failure mode this repo has
produced three times already.
Thresholds are set from the SWA preview measurement -- the application's
real performance on a real deployment -- and every one of them is met
today, so this gate is green on arrival rather than aspirational.
NEVER POINT THESE ASSERTIONS AT THE APEX. Permanent, not conditional.
The apex scores 16 performance and 19 best-practices points below the
IDENTICAL build on the SWA origin; the gap is Cloudflare's Bot Management
JS Detections, which on the Free plan is mandatory and cannot be disabled,
scoped, or skipped. Decided 2026-07-30 as accepted/won't-fix -- see
docs/strategy/plans/PLAN-015-cloudflare-bot-management.md.
This note used to read `until that is resolved`. It IS resolved, and the
apex still cannot pass -- a resolved item is not necessarily a fixed one.
Only a Cloudflare plan upgrade would change the answer, never a code
change. The guard in __tests__/infra/lighthouse-config.test.ts enforces
this by failing if `collect.url` is ever set.
